steps.body: Small shapes **build** big ones! Two triangles can make a square. Six squares wrap into a cube.

widget.prompt: You snap two same-size triangles together along their longest sides. Tap what they can make.

hotspots.label: a circle
hotspots.feedback: Circles have no straight edges to snap — triangles make a square.

hotspots.label: a bigger triangle only
hotspots.feedback: They CAN also make a square — joined on the long side!

widget.missFeedback: Shapes love to combine — these two make a square.
widget.successFeedback: Yes — two triangles join into a square.

steps.body: Look for shapes **inside** shapes. A house drawing is a triangle sitting on a square!

explanationVariants: A house drawing is a square (walls) with a triangle (roof) on top.

widget.prompt: A drawing of a house has walls and a pointy roof. Which two shapes build it?

options.label: Two circles
options.feedback: Circles are round — walls are a square, the roof a triangle.

options.label: A square and a circle
options.feedback: The pointy roof is a TRIANGLE, not a circle.

options.label: Two triangles
options.feedback: The walls are square — one triangle is just the roof.

widget.prompt: You have two same-size squares. You put them side by side. Tap what they make.

hotspots.label: a rectangle — two squares in a row
a triangle
hotspots.feedback: Squares have zero points to give — side by side they make a rectangle.

hotspots.label: a bigger square
hotspots.feedback: Side by side they are twice as WIDE — that is a rectangle.

widget.missFeedback: All the edges stay straight — they make a rectangle.
widget.successFeedback: Yes — two squares in a row make a rectangle.

explanationVariants: Two triangles → square; two squares → rectangle; six squares fold into a cube.
Each build uses its parts' edges.

widget.prompt: Match the pieces to what they build.

pairErrors.feedback: Two squares side by side get WIDER — that is a rectangle, not a square.

widget.missFeedback: Think about each build: triangles pair into a square; squares line into a rectangle; six squares wrap a cube.
widget.successFeedback: All built — small shapes make big ones!

explanationVariants: A sail is the triangle; the boat bottom is the half-circle-like curve — the triangle is the pointy part.
The pointy sail is a triangle.

widget.prompt: A drawing of a sailboat has a pointy sail. Tap the shape of the sail.

hotspots.label: square
hotspots.feedback: Squares have four even sides — the pointy sail is a triangle.

hotspots.label: circle
hotspots.feedback: Circles have no points — the sail is a triangle.

hotspots.label: rectangle
hotspots.feedback: Rectangles are boxy — the pointy sail is a triangle.

widget.missFeedback: Look for the shape with a point at the top — that is the sail.
widget.successFeedback: Yes — the pointy sail is a triangle.

steps.body: Sort the builds by what they make.
explanationVariants: Two triangles make a square, three squares in a row make a rectangle, and six squares fold into a cube.
Small shapes build big ones: triangles join into a square, a row of squares grows into a rectangle, six squares wrap into a cube.

widget.prompt: Put each set of pieces under the shape it can build.

items.label: two same-size triangles joined on their long sides
items.feedback: Those triangles can make a square.

items.label: three same-size squares in one row
items.feedback: A row gets longer than it is tall, making a rectangle.

items.label: six square faces folded into a closed box
items.feedback: Six square faces can wrap around to make a cube.

widget.missFeedback: Think about the outside edge of each finished build.
widget.successFeedback: Yes — small shapes can be joined to build new shapes!

hints: Two triangles can fit together into one square.
Squares in a row make a longer shape — a rectangle.
Six flat squares fold up into a box — a cube.

steps.body: Small shapes combine into bigger shapes — look for shapes inside shapes.
takeaways: Two triangles make a square; two squares make a rectangle.
Drawings hide shapes: a house is a square plus a triangle.
Building with shapes is math you can touch.
steps.teaser: Next chapter: comparing and sorting everything!

concept.body: Small shapes build big ones. Two triangles make a square. A house is a square with a triangle roof.

explanationVariants: Two triangles snap into a square.

widget.prompt: Which pieces can build a square?

options.label: Two triangles
options.feedback: Yes — two triangles make a square.

options.label: Two circles
options.feedback: Circles have no straight edges — two TRIANGLES build a square.

options.label: One circle and one triangle
options.feedback: The round side will not fit — two triangles do it.

options.label: Nothing can
options.feedback: Two triangles can — snap them on their long sides!
